I've had my IPV4 for about a month now, I did a first impressions shortly after getting it but was sick (some kind of flu like crap that turned into a chest infection) and wasn't able to really vape it. I finally started feeling better a couple weeks ago and have been able to play with it enough to do an informed review.

I'm not going to go over appearance etc again since I covered that here in first impressions

There's been a lot of talk about the charging board insulator and fires, I've had 0 issues with mine and being almost terminally lazy I think I won't bother removing it. Based on what I read various places it looks like the issue was primarily popping up in earlier batches especially the silver. While I do not think it is solely responsible for the charging board shorts I think modding early silver IPV4 devices to remove the tint on the screen did play a part in the high frequency of issues that were occurring a month ago. I haven't seen any new reports of issues in the past couple weeks (if I'm wrong let me know so I can edit this) so it's possible that the issue has been resolved in newer batches. Nor have I experienced any of the other electrical issues reported with the black IPV4 mods, mine's been rock solid. In my experience (based on my device and the devices belonging to 2 of my friends) as long as you follow basic safety/best practices for a dual battery device the IPV4 is a reasonably safe device (that being said 3 devices is not a statistically valid sample for evaluating the performance/safety of a mass produced product, so make you're own call based on all the available information).

Performance has been great. I rarely use the device past about 45-50W where the tanks/drippers I use seem to work best for me. I have had it up in the 75-100w range for a while and it runs well at the high end. Battery life is amazing since I'm usually either vaping @ 35-45w or 40j and I'll easily get 2-3 days out of it. Since the battery life is longer than my attention and I always forget to check the battery indicator there have been a few times I've found myself with no charged spares and almost dead batteries. The menu is intuitive and easy to use, 5 fire button taps to get to the menu, +/- to make changes and tapping the fire button in the menu cycles between menu items, and the menu time out is fairly generous.

The IPV4 is my first temp control mod, so I had to pick up some Ni200 wire and have been running 6 wrap 26g @ 400F, 40j in my derringer clone the past week, and the temp control feature has worked perfectly. I can't really compare it to the temp control of other boards dna40 etc as I haven't used them, but I can say that I will continue to use Ni wire and temp control in my RDAs, I love not having to worry about dry hits.

Overall, I'm very happy with the device, honestly I was really worried and questioning my purchase when I got it because of all the reports of issues in /r/electronic_cigarette I'm usually that guy who gets the bad unit even in devices with out a history of problems so I was expecting to have to RMA it at some point. Performance has been great and all the IPV4s belonging to either my friends or myself have had no issues. If it were not for all the reports of issues from early batches I'd have 0 issue recommending this device, it's a great step up from the entry level enthusiast devices (stuff like the kanger sub box), or older less capable mods. As it is I'm a bit conflicted about a recommendation, mine's been great, my friends have been great but 3 devices is very small sample and the issues reported are in the very bad to catastrophically bad category (dead mod to house fire range) my suggestion would be to skip the IPV4 and get an IPV4S which is the manufacturer's attempt to address the reported deficiencies of the original IPV4 and comes with out the balance board.
